books.title: Second Treatise of Government
books.author: John Locke
books.description: The founding text of liberal political philosophy: government by consent, natural rights to life, liberty, and property, and the people's right to dissolve a government that betrays its trust. All 243 sections in modern English.

books.title: Hamlet, Prince of Denmark
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.description: Shakespeare's tragedy of revenge, conscience, and delay, rendered act by act into modern English — every speech, scene, and stage direction.

books.title: The Social Contract (Books I–II)
books.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
books.description: “Man is born free; and everywhere he is in chains.” Rousseau's account of legitimate political authority — the social compact, the sovereign, and the general will — from G. D. H. Cole's translation, modernized.

books.title: The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire (Chapters XV–XVI)
books.author: Edward Gibbon
books.description: Gibbon's two most famous — and most notorious — chapters: the rise of Christianity and the conduct of Rome toward the Christians, with the irony fully intact.
